name: struts2-s2-001
notes: The control is class attribution: the same vulnerable target, probed for the
wrong class, must come back clean. S2-001 re-evaluates submitted values as
OGNL -- there is no shell behind it -- so the shell-syntax probes of `reflected`
have nothing to execute. A tool that confirmed here would be flagging the
parameter, not the class. Measured: 844 probes, all negative.
`password` is not padding. The login action throws before it re-renders the
form unless both fields are present, so a POST carrying only `username` gets
HTTP 500 and the injected value is never evaluated. This case sent exactly
that and reported `negative` from 700 probes against a target that is
vulnerable -- the benchmark's own false negative, and the reason the form is
read off the running app rather than guessed.
Verified against vulhub struts2/s2-001 on 2026-09-19: the form posts to
/login.action with fields `username` and `password`; POSTing both returns 200
with %{333*3} rendered as 999 in value="999". RCEKit then confirms with 70 of
--build is in the compose command because vulhub's s2-001 ships a Dockerfile.
